title: Loop readiness, negotiation, Branch A/B plan + Phase 7 gate
objective: Interview loop readiness (debrief ritual, project interrogation), negotiation prep with market bands, the two-branch plan (interviews live / no traction yet), final polish of flagship READMEs and case studies, Phase 7 assessment.
topics: Loop shape: 2–3 coding, 1 behavioral, SD at L4+
Negotiation: anchors, competing offers, comp structure
Branch A (interviews live) / Branch B (take the strongest offer as the platform)
theory: Blueprint Sheet 04; reference CI-3 offer basics; career-trajectory-playbook negotiation.
deliverables: docs/negotiation.md with market bands per role family

knowledge: What is your walk-away number and why?
Which branch are you on today?
practical: Phase 7 gate pass criteria all met

tasks.text: docs/interview-loop.md: per round — clarify aloud before coding, narrate approach, test edge cases before declaring done; behavioral rubric; SD round structure. Debrief within the hour after every real round.
Timed coding session (2 mediums / 45 min) + 5 cold re-solves from top100.

docs/negotiation.md: never anchor on current CTC; market bands for your unlocked level (from the reference tables); base + variable + ESOP/RSU evaluation; competing processes in the same window; everything in writing. Rehearse the conversation once with a friend.
Case study 1 (PairCraft): problem → architecture → numbers → failures → what changed; 600 words + diagram.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.

docs/plan-branch-a-b.md: Branch A — interviews live: weekly cadence, debrief, drills. Branch B — no traction by month 12 (normal): take the strongest offer as the platform; keep DSA 3–4 h/week; keep projects alive; Quiet Network continues; lateral shot in 12–18 months.
Full SD mock (45 min, software) + AI design mock (45 min) — or one of each across today/tomorrow. Record; deltas.
Quiet Network: 1–2 genuine conversations with engineers from your target list (thoughtful comment or a question about their work; no pitch, no referral ask). Log in the tracker.
Take the Phase 7 gate (Assessments → P7): coding checks, SD + AI mocks passed, capstone + blog live, tracker ≥20 rows, 2-minute intro + 3-minute flagship pitches recorded. Record.
Application pipeline (20 min): check saved searches, apply to 1–2 fitting roles within 48 h of posting, update tracker (status · next action · what failed).
Passed → tick m-interview; phase review. Failed → W52 becomes the “fail → revisit” week for the failed part.

Weekly revision — Loop shape: 2–3 coding, 1 behavioral, SD at L4+, Post-round debrief ritual, Negotiation: anchors, competing offers, comp structure, Branch A (interviews live) / Branch B (take the strongest offer as the platform): rewrite the key ideas from memory (no notes), then compare with your notes and fix the gaps. Reimplement two things from this week without looking.
DSA second pass · cold re-solve: Longest Increasing Subsequence (Medium, B75) · Partition Equal Subset Sum (Medium) — ≤35 min each, narrate, log time.
Weekly review: answer this week’s knowledge questions aloud, run the practical checks, then write the three notes (struggled / learned / improve) in Weekly Plan → Review. Update the tracking sheet.

JS/MERN spaced recall (Cycle 3 · interview mode) · TypeScript for MERN: Interview mode: explain interface vs type, unknown vs any, generics with constraints in 2 min each; type a custom hook. Log misses in mistakes.md; if you fail the check, redo the matching module in Side Tracks → 🟨 JavaScript & MERN Refresher.
Plan next week: read W52’s objective and Day 1; move any unfinished 🔴 task into next week’s Day 1; confirm calendar blocks. Then rest — consistency beats intensity.
